title: Earth2Studio.jl
text:
Overview
Welcome to the documentation for Earth2Studio.jl.
Earth2Studio.jl is a Julia wrapper around NVIDIA’s earth2studio Python package for AI-powered weather and climate forecasting. It provides:
The package uses PythonCall.jl and CondaPkg.jl to manage the Python environment automatically.

title: Earth2Studio.jl
text:
Data Sources: Access ERA5 reanalysis, GFS forecasts, HRRR, and more via a unified interface.
Prognostic Models: Run state-of-the-art AI weather models including FourCastNet, Pangu-Weather, GraphCast, Aurora, and AIFS.
Diagnostic Models: Apply downscaling (CorrDiff), precipitation estimation, tropical cyclone tracking, and derived quantities.
Ensemble Forecasting: Generate perturbed ensemble members with Gaussian, bred vector, and lagged ensemble methods.
Verification Metrics: Compute RMSE, ACC, CRPS, Brier scores, and more.

title: Earth2Studio.jl
text:
Quickstart
using Pkg
Pkg.add(url="https://github.com/RallypointOne/Earth2Studio.jl")
The base package installs lightweight Python dependencies (numpy, xarray). To use AI models, add earth2studio with the desired extras to your project’s CondaPkg.toml:
[pip.deps]
"earth2studio[pangu]" = ""
Then run a deterministic forecast:
using Earth2Studio
using Dates

# Load data and model
data = GFS()
model = Pangu24()
io = ZarrBackend("/tmp/forecast.zarr")

# Run a 10-step forecast from a specific date
result = run_deterministic(DateTime(2024, 1, 15), 10, model, data, io)

# Convert results to Julia arrays
ds = to_xarray(result)

title: Tutorial
text:
Setup
This tutorial walks through a complete weather forecasting workflow with Earth2Studio.jl: fetching initial conditions, running a forecast, and visualizing results.
using Earth2Studio
using Dates

title: Tutorial
text:
Step 1: Fetch Initial Conditions
Choose a data source and fetch fields for a given time and set of variables:

ds = WB2ERA5()
result = fetch_data(ds, DateTime(2024, 6, 15), ["t2m", "u10m", "v10m"])

result.data    # Array{Float32, 4} with dims (time, variable, lat, lon)
result.dims    # (:time, :variable, :lat, :lon)
result.coords  # NamedTuple with lat/lon vectors, etc.

title: Tutorial
text:
Step 2: Run a Deterministic Forecast
Load a prognostic model and run a 10-step forecast:

model = Pangu24()
to_device!(model, "cuda")

io = ZarrBackend("/tmp/forecast.zarr")

result = run_deterministic(DateTime(2024, 6, 15), 10, model, ds, io)
ds_out = to_xarray(result)

title: Tutorial
text:
Step 3: Visualize the Forecast

Global Temperature Field
A snapshot of 2-meter temperature at a single forecast lead time. Earth2Studio returns data on a regular latitude-longitude grid.

lat = collect(range(90, -90, length=181))
lon = collect(range(0, 359, length=360))

# Synthetic T2m field: warm tropics, cold poles, land-sea contrast
t2m = [
    280.0 + 25.0 * cosd(la) +
    3.0 * sind(2lo) * cosd(la) +
    5.0 * sind(3la) * cosd(2lo) +
    2.0 * cosd(5lo + 2la)
    for la in lat, lo in lon
]

fig = Figure(size=(900, 450))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1],
    xlabel="Longitude (°)", ylabel="Latitude (°)",
    title="2m Temperature — 24h Forecast (2024-06-16 00Z)",
)
hm = heatmap!(ax, lon, lat, t2m', colormap=Reverse(:RdBu), colorrange=(235, 315))
Colorbar(fig[1, 2], hm, label="Temperature (K)")
fig






Figure 2.1: 2-meter temperature (K) — 24-hour forecast valid 2024-06-16 00Z






Forecast Time Series
Track a variable at a single grid point across forecast lead times.

hours = 0:6:240
n = length(hours)

# Synthetic forecast: diurnal cycle + slight warm drift
t2m_fcst = 288.0 .+ 4.0 .* sin.(2π .* hours ./ 24) .+ 0.015 .* hours .+ 0.8 .* randn(n)

# Synthetic "truth": same diurnal cycle, no drift
t2m_era5 = 288.0 .+ 4.0 .* sin.(2π .* hours ./ 24) .+ 0.5 .* randn(n)

fig = Figure(size=(800, 400))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1],
    xlabel="Lead time (hours)", ylabel="Temperature (K)",
    title="T2m Forecast vs. ERA5 — Paris (48.9°N, 2.3°E)",
)
lines!(ax, hours, t2m_era5, label="ERA5 analysis", color=:gray30, linewidth=2)
lines!(ax, hours, t2m_fcst, label="Pangu24 forecast", color=:steelblue, linewidth=2)
axislegend(ax, position=:lt)
fig






Figure 2.2: 48-hour T2m forecast at a single grid point vs. ERA5 analysis






Ensemble Spread
Run an ensemble forecast to quantify uncertainty:

io_ens = ZarrBackend("/tmp/ensemble.zarr")
perturb = SphericalGaussian()
result = run_ensemble(DateTime(2024, 6, 15), 40, 10, model, ds, io_ens, perturb)

Visualize the ensemble envelope:

hours_ens = 0:6:240
n_ens = length(hours_ens)
n_members = 10

# Synthetic ensemble: members diverge over time
base = 288.0 .+ 4.0 .* sin.(2π .* hours_ens ./ 24)
members = hcat([base .+ cumsum(0.3 .* randn(n_ens)) for _ in 1:n_members]...)

ens_mean = vec(mean(members, dims=2))
ens_min = vec(minimum(members, dims=2))
ens_max = vec(maximum(members, dims=2))
ens_p25 = vec(mapslices(x -> sort(x)[3], members, dims=2))
ens_p75 = vec(mapslices(x -> sort(x)[8], members, dims=2))

fig = Figure(size=(800, 400))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1],
    xlabel="Lead time (hours)", ylabel="Temperature (K)",
    title="Ensemble Forecast — T2m at Paris (48.9°N, 2.3°E)",
)
band!(ax, hours_ens, ens_min, ens_max, color=(:steelblue, 0.15), label="Min–Max")
band!(ax, hours_ens, ens_p25, ens_p75, color=(:steelblue, 0.3), label="25th–75th pct")
lines!(ax, hours_ens, ens_mean, color=:steelblue, linewidth=2.5, label="Ensemble mean")
axislegend(ax, position=:lt)
fig






Figure 2.3: 10-member ensemble forecast of T2m showing spread growth with lead time






Verification: RMSE by Lead Time
Compare forecast skill across models:

hours_v = 0:6:240
n_v = length(hours_v)

# Synthetic RMSE curves: persistence grows fast, AI models grow slowly
rmse_persist = 10.0 .+ 3.5 .* sqrt.(hours_v)
rmse_pangu   = 10.0 .+ 0.8 .* hours_v .^ 0.65
rmse_gcst    = 12.0 .+ 0.7 .* hours_v .^ 0.65
rmse_fcn     = 14.0 .+ 1.0 .* hours_v .^ 0.65

fig = Figure(size=(800, 400))
ax = Axis(fig[1, 1],
    xlabel="Lead time (hours)", ylabel="RMSE (m²/s²)",
    title="Z500 RMSE — Global",
)
lines!(ax, hours_v, rmse_persist, label="Persistence", color=:gray60, linewidth=2, linestyle=:dash)
lines!(ax, hours_v, rmse_pangu, label="Pangu24", color=:steelblue, linewidth=2)
lines!(ax, hours_v, rmse_gcst, label="GraphCast", color=:firebrick, linewidth=2)
lines!(ax, hours_v, rmse_fcn, label="FourCastNet", color=:goldenrod, linewidth=2)
axislegend(ax, position=:lt)
fig






Figure 2.4: Global RMSE of 500 hPa geopotential height by lead time

title: Data Sources
text:
Fetching Data
All data sources are callable. Pass a time (or vector of times) and variable name(s):
using Earth2Studio, Dates

ds = WB2ERA5()

# Fetch a single variable at one time
da = ds(DateTime(2024, 1, 1), "t2m")

# Fetch multiple variables at multiple times
da = ds([DateTime(2024, 1, 1), DateTime(2024, 1, 2)], ["t2m", "u10m", "v10m"])

title: Data Sources
text:
Converting to Julia Arrays
Use fetch_data for a one-call Julia-native result:
result = fetch_data(ds, DateTime(2024, 1, 1), ["t2m", "msl"])

result.data    # Array of values
result.dims    # e.g. (:time, :variable, :lat, :lon)
result.coords  # NamedTuple of coordinate vectors
Or use xarray_to_dict on any xarray DataArray:
da = ds(DateTime(2024, 1, 1), "t2m")
result = xarray_to_dict(da)

text:

Construct from any earth2studio.data class name:
ds = DataSource("CDS"; kwargs...)

title: Models
text:
Prognostic Models
Earth2Studio.jl wraps two categories of AI weather models: prognostic models that step the atmosphere forward in time, and diagnostic models that derive additional quantities from the forecast state.
Prognostic models produce multi-step weather forecasts. Each constructor downloads pretrained weights on first use.

title: Workflows
text:
Deterministic Forecast
Earth2Studio.jl provides three standard forecast workflows. Each writes results into an IO backend and returns it for further analysis.
Run a single-member forecast:
Arguments:

title: Workflows
text:
using Earth2Studio, Dates

data = GFS()
model = Pangu24()
io = ZarrBackend("/tmp/deterministic.zarr")

result = run_deterministic(DateTime(2024, 1, 1), 10, model, data, io)
ds = to_xarray(result)


time: Initial time (DateTime, Date, or vector)
nsteps: Number of forecast steps
prognostic: A PrognosticModel
data: A DataSource
io: An IOBackend
device (keyword): "cuda" or "cpu" (default: model’s current device)

title: Workflows
text:
Ensemble Forecast
Run a multi-member ensemble with perturbations:
data = GFS()
model = Pangu24()
io = ZarrBackend("/tmp/ensemble.zarr")
perturb = Gaussian()

result = run_ensemble(DateTime(2024, 1, 1), 10, 4, model, data, io, perturb)
ds = to_xarray(result)
Additional arguments:

nensemble: Number of ensemble members
perturbation: A Perturbation method
batch_size (keyword): GPU batch size (default: nensemble)

title: Workflows
text:
Diagnostic Forecast
Apply a diagnostic model at each forecast step:
data = GFS()
px_model = Pangu24()
dx_model = PrecipitationAFNO()
io = ZarrBackend("/tmp/diagnostic.zarr")

result = run_diagnostic(DateTime(2024, 1, 1), 10, px_model, dx_model, data, io)
ds = to_xarray(result)

title: Statistics

Usage
Construct a metric with reduction dimensions, then call it on forecast and observation data:
metric = RMSE(reduction_dimensions=["lat", "lon"])
score = metric(forecast_da, observation_da)

title: API
text:
DataSource


DataSource
Wrapper around an earth2studio.data.* Python data source object.
Construct via named constructors like ARCO, GFS, etc.
DataSource(class_name::AbstractString; kwargs...)
Construct a DataSource from an arbitrary earth2studio.data class name.

Examples
ds = DataSource("CDS")





DiagnosticModel


DiagnosticModel
Wrapper around an earth2studio.models.dx.* diagnostic model.
Construct via named constructors like CorrDiff, ClimateNet, etc.
DiagnosticModel(class_name::AbstractString; kwargs...)
Construct a DiagnosticModel from an arbitrary earth2studio.models.dx class name.

Examples
model = DiagnosticModel("CorrDiff")





IOBackend


IOBackend
Wrapper around an earth2studio.io.* IO backend for storing forecast results.
Construct via named constructors like ZarrBackend, NetCDF4Backend, etc.
IOBackend(class_name::AbstractString, args...; kwargs...)
Construct an IOBackend from an arbitrary earth2studio.io class name.

Examples
io = IOBackend("ZarrBackend", "/tmp/output.zarr")





Perturbation


Perturbation
Wrapper around an earth2studio.perturbation.* perturbation method.
Construct via named constructors like Gaussian, Zero, etc.
Perturbation(class_name::AbstractString; kwargs...)
Construct a Perturbation from an arbitrary earth2studio.perturbation class name.

Examples
p = Perturbation("Gaussian"; noise_amplitude=0.05)





PrognosticModel


PrognosticModel
Wrapper around an earth2studio.models.px.* prognostic (forecast) model.
Construct via named constructors like FourCastNet, Pangu24, etc.
PrognosticModel(class_name::AbstractString; kwargs...)
Construct a PrognosticModel from an arbitrary earth2studio.models.px class name.

Examples
model = PrognosticModel("FCN")

Run a deterministic forecast for nsteps time steps. Returns the IOBackend containing results.

Examples
io = run_deterministic(DateTime(2024, 1, 1), 10, model, data, ZarrBackend("/tmp/out.zarr"))
ds = to_xarray(io)





run_diagnostic


run_diagnostic(time, nsteps, prognostic, diagnostic, data, io; device=nothing, kwargs...)
Run a forecast with a diagnostic model applied at each step. Returns the IOBackend containing results.

Examples
io = run_diagnostic(DateTime(2024,1,1), 10, px_model, dx_model, data, ZarrBackend("/tmp/out.zarr"))
ds = to_xarray(io)





run_ensemble


run_ensemble(time, nsteps, nensemble, prognostic, data, io, perturbation; batch_size=nothing, device=nothing, kwargs...)
Run an ensemble forecast with nensemble members. Returns the IOBackend containing results.

Examples
io = run_ensemble(DateTime(2024,1,1), 10, 4, model, data, ZarrBackend("/tmp/out.zarr"), Zero())
ds = to_xarray(io)





to_device! {#to_device!}


to_device!(model, device::AbstractString)
Move a prognostic or diagnostic model to the specified device (e.g. "cuda", "cpu").

Examples
model = Pangu24()
to_device!(model, "cuda")





to_xarray


to_xarray(io::IOBackend)
Return the xarray Dataset stored in an IOBackend after a workflow run completes.

Examples
io = ZarrBackend("/tmp/forecast.zarr")
io = run_deterministic(time, 10, model, data, io)
ds = to_xarray(io)





xarray_to_dict


xarray_to_dict(da::Py) -> NamedTuple
Convert an xarray DataArray to a Julia NamedTuple with fields data, dims, and coords.

Examples
result = fetch_data(ds, DateTime(2024,1,1), "t2m")
result.data   # Array of values
result.dims   # (:time, :variable, :lat, :lon)
result.coords # NamedTuple of coordinate vectors
